players.product: Power transformers and substation / transmission-and-distribution equipment, including SF6 gas-free products; Numazu transformer plant expansion to about 1.5x capacity

quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal year ended March 2026 (fiscal 2025, the first year of Medium-term Management Plan 2027): net sales JPY 326,194 million (up 8.3%), operating income JPY 27,122 million (up 26.1%), ordinary income JPY 27,889 million (up 31.6%), net income attributable to owners of the parent JPY 23,625 million (up 27.8%), ROE 15.1%, ROIC 9.4%; sales and operating income were record highs, and operating income beat the initial plan of JPY 20,000 million (revised plan JPY 24,000 million). Orders received JPY 358,239 million (93.4% of the prior year), the second-highest after the record fiscal 2024, including the order for India's high-speed rail line 1. Management attributes the results to strong demand centred on the Power Infrastructure business, price optimisation and cost reduction lifting the social infrastructure businesses, and growing recurring maintenance revenue. Sales by customer location: Japan JPY 235,342 million, Asia JPY 61,256 million, other regions JPY 29,596 million; no single customer reaches 10% of net sales
quarterly_data.figure: net sales JPY 326,194 million (+8.3%); operating income JPY 27,122 million (+26.1%); net income JPY 23,625 million (+27.8%); orders JPY 358,239 million

quarterly_data.signal: Order backlog at March 31, 2026: JPY 411,933 million in total (110.0% of the prior year), of which Power Infrastructure JPY 179,365 million (113.4%), Social Systems JPY 181,382 million (112.3%), Industrial, Electronic and Mobility JPY 30,062 million (86.9%) and Field Engineering JPY 19,550 million (108.2%). Orders received by segment: Power Infrastructure JPY 115,693 million (92.3%), Social Systems JPY 116,351 million (99.0%), Industrial, Electronic and Mobility JPY 64,507 million (76.2%), Field Engineering JPY 55,256 million (112.5%)
quarterly_data.figure: order backlog JPY 411,933 million (110.0%); Power Infrastructure backlog JPY 179,365 million (113.4%)

quarterly_data.signal: Power Infrastructure segment, fiscal year ended March 2026: net sales up 16.7% to JPY 100,844 million and operating income improved by JPY 4,596 million to JPY 12,584 million, both record highs. The mainly overseas substation business grew sales and income on demand growth in the U.S., Singapore and elsewhere plus profitability improvements; the mainly domestic Power & Energy business grew on rising demand from electric power company projects. Segment production JPY 97,691 million (115.6% of the prior year)
quarterly_data.figure: net sales JPY 100,844 million (+16.7%); operating income JPY 12,584 million; production JPY 97,691 million (115.6%)

quarterly_data.signal: Capex in the fiscal year ended March 2026 included expanding the large-transformer test area and refurbishing drying furnaces to strengthen the existing transformer plant lines, plus plant infrastructure at Numazu Works; Power Infrastructure capex included substation-product facilities JPY 4,547 million and generation-product facilities JPY 434 million, and other plants are investing in capacity for operation from fiscal 2026 onward. Medium-term plan progress in fiscal 2025: strengthened vacuum capacitor production equipment (phased operation from fiscal 2027) and decided to relocate and consolidate the substation equipment plant in Singapore (operation planned in fiscal 2028); the plan targets JPY 130 hundred million or more of capex each for substation / electronics capacity in Japan and for strengthening and restructuring overseas sites, plus 25% higher production capacity and 50% shorter lead times through DX. Next year's Power Infrastructure capex plan includes substation-product facilities of JPY 12,162 million and generation-product facilities of JPY 284 million
quarterly_data.figure: substation-product capex JPY 4,547 million; next-year substation-product capex plan JPY 12,162 million; Singapore plant from fiscal 2028

quarterly_data.signal: Product and market progress in fiscal 2025 (year ended March 2026): completed development of a 123kV eco-tank vacuum circuit breaker (VCB) and started selling it in North America; launched a new power conditioning system (PCS) model for grid battery systems; set development specifications for vacuum interrupters (VI) and VCBs for the European market and began full-scale sales activity with a local marketing organisation; began shipping substation equipment for India's high-speed rail line 1; won new development projects from North American semiconductor-related customers. R&D spending JPY 13,473 million (4.1% of net sales; Power Infrastructure JPY 2,006 million), raising the voltage and capacity of SF6-free dry-air vacuum circuit breakers and developing high-efficiency, compact AC/DC converters using high-frequency transformers for power systems expected to spread with data center power demand; core technologies for solid-state transformers (SST) were evaluated
quarterly_data.figure: 123kV VCB; R&D JPY 13,473 million (4.1% of net sales)

quarterly_data.signal: Management states global power demand is rising further with AI / data center expansion, electrification and faster renewable adoption, and equipment-renewal and maintenance / service demand is expected to run above initial assumptions; it cites Middle East tension, China's export restrictions on critical minerals, U.S. tariffs and sharp FX moves as major uncertainties, and a slowdown in EV market growth. Operating income is progressing ahead of the Medium-term Management Plan 2027, a trend management expects to continue next year. Initial plan for the fiscal year ending March 2027: orders JPY 375,000 million, net sales JPY 355,000 million, operating income JPY 29,000 million, assuming USD 1 = JPY 150. Plan 2027 targets for the fiscal year ending March 2028: orders JPY 380,000 million, net sales JPY 370,000 million, operating income JPY 25,000 million (6.8% margin), ROE 10.0%, ROIC 8.0%
quarterly_data.figure: FY plan orders JPY 375,000 million; net sales JPY 355,000 million; operating income JPY 29,000 million; MTP target net sales JPY 370,000 million
